descricao_original: Most of the small intestine protrudes into an internal body cavity, the peritoneal cavity, and is therefore, covered by a serosa, consisting of a simple squamous epithelium (mesothelium) and a small amount of connective tissue. This serosa, called visceral peritoneum, produces a lubricating fluid that reduces friction between the organs. A portion of the duodenum is retroperitoneal, covered only on its anterior surface by a serosa. The posterior surface, where it contacts the posterior body wall, has an adventitia only. 800x
